comment: Every role the package disagrees with, and what was decided about it.
Exact equality, not a ratchet down: a new disagreement and a resolved one both fail, because both
are a decision somebody has to record. Re-bank deliberately with UPDATE_ROLES_BASELINE=1 pnpm test,
and fill in the decision - a banked entry without one fails too.
verdict   cross-family   - the package uses this role, but only for a slot of another kind
family-conflict - the package paints this slot from another family entirely
decision  confirmed   - the package assigns this very role here; only our slot word differs
naming      - the role is right for what the property paints; the slot word is not
rule-5      - one value in two roles, named after the dominant one (DIVERGENCES)
bridge      - built with rgb(from role / a); the foundation names no role for it
package-gap - no role of the right family exists; a request, not a swap
design      - a correction would move a pixel, so it is not ours to make
typographyUnmarked - typography step reads that carry no marker at all. The px gate only looks at
literals, so a step read slipped past it; these are banked until each one is routed to a role or
marked with a reason.
slotLies - the slot word contradicts the CSS property the bundle shows it painting. Same rules as
above: banked with a decision, exact equality. hairline and rule-5 are deliberate and stay; naming
is a rename wave waiting for a changelog, not a role defect.
ladders - a slot whose states resolve to one role. `focused` reusing `hovered` is accepted
convention and never listed. decision no-rung means the system has no role for the second state
either; design means it does and we skip it.
contrast - foreground and background the bundle puts in ONE rule, resolved per mode. Alpha-bridge
values and disabled selectors are excluded: the first renders as a tint over an unknown surface,
the second is exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 and gated by disabled-paint.test.ts. decision graphic-ok means
the pair is a glyph and clears 3:1; design means it misses the threshold that applies to it.
concepts - one anatomical concept (modifiers + slot + state, sub-elements dropped) painted with
several roles across components. This is the only check that asks the question the task is named
after; every other one reads a single declaration. decision spelling means the roles resolve to one
colour and differ only in family, shade means same family different value, design means the
components disagree about the colour itself.
judgmentCalls - where the decision was not read off the package or a standard. Kept because a
fixed item leaves the lists above and its reasoning would leave with it.

Widened 09.09 after asking whether danger passes anywhere else. It does not, and the reason is that the role is tuned to one surface. In dark content-danger is danger-80 #e4554f, and it measures 4.58 on the page canvas (bg-canvas #1d1d1d), 4.22 on an ordinary surface (bg #242424) and 3.05 on a hovered one (bg-hovered #3b3b3b). So it clears AA on the canvas by 0.08 and fails everywhere below it. Eleven theme variables put real text on this role - the outlined danger button label, the chat alert list, the chat delete item, the fieldset invalid value, the grid AI error, the informer error, two stepper invalid labels, the text editor invalid message, the validation message and the validation summary - and every one of them sits at 4.22 wherever its widget has its own background. Three more read the role for a glyph (diagram, filterBuilder, cardView), where 4.22 clears the 3:1 that applies. The request splits in two: on an ordinary surface the miss is 0.28 and one ramp step fixes it - danger-70 #ee726a gives 5.36 - so ask the package to move content-danger in dark; on a hovered surface nothing in the family clears AA, danger-70 reaching only 3.87, so that half is a genuine gap. Light is fine throughout (6.07 on the canvas, 5.56 hovered). Why the audit saw one row and not twelve: the rule-local pass needs both colours in one rule, and a validation message takes its background from an ancestor. Third instance of that blind spot in one day.

comment: Why a contrast pair below AA does not turn the dark a11y job red. Asked 09.09.2026 and grounded
in axe-core 4.12.1 source rather than assumed - the answer is structural, so it applies to every
future finding of the same shape.

reasons.reason: axe reads DOM text nodes, and an icon glyph is not one
reasons.detail: visibleTextNodes() in axe-core collects children with nodeType === 3. DevExtreme icon fonts render through ::before { content: "\fXXX" }, which is generated content, not a child node - so an element whose only text is a glyph never enters the color-contrast rule. The splitter grip is exactly that: dx-icon-sizing sets a font-size on .dx-resize-handle-icon and the glyph arrives from the icon font.
reasons.covers: every chevron, checkmark, arrow, grip and spinner in the theme

reasons.reason: WCAG 1.4.11 has no axe rule at all
reasons.detail: Non-text contrast - 3:1 for control boundaries and graphics - is not implemented in axe. Borders, focus rings, indicators and switch tracks are outside the gate by construction, not by suppression. Сплошной проверки нетекстового контраста в теме тоже нет: 09.09 так был померен только сплиттер, и по его результату вопрос Д7 закрыт 15.09 - таблица тех замеров ушла со страницы вместе с ним, потому что описывала сплиттер, которого больше нет.
reasons.covers: the whole non-text half of the contrast requirement

reasons.reason: the state has to be reached
reasons.detail: The delete item in the message-list context menu measures 3.05 in dark, and it is real text - but only while the menu is open and that item focused. A pair that needs a state the a11y suite never enters is invisible even when the rule applies to it.
reasons.covers: findings in transient states: focused, opened, invalid

whyContrastDoesNotFailCi.consequence: Тёмный a11y-прогон идёт и color-contrast в нём включён - но он видит только настоящий текст в достижимых состояниях. Контраст глифов и нетекстовых элементов не проверяет никто, и таблица контраста в этом отчёте - единственное место, где он измерен.

checkbox-focused-fill.why:
Resolved in part on 15.09, when the designer produced the package tokens for checkbox/color/checked. Three slots, not one: border, bg and icon each have their own token, and our theme painted the border from the BG variable. Figma and Blazor agree that the border is border-primary-shared*, so that half was not a judgement call and is applied - three new names, light pixel-identical (primary-100/120/140 exactly as before), dark better at every rung: the box outline against the page goes 2.88 -> 4.65 at rest, 3.69 -> 5.79 hovered, 1.39 -> 1.98 pressed.
WHAT REMAINS. The fill. Figma says bg-primary*, Blazor implements content-primary-shared*, and the two are identical in light and differ in dark - which is exactly what decides this row. On Figma's fill the mark reads 3.36 at rest and 1.62 pressed; on Blazor's, 5.42 and 2.31. Neither clears 3.0 in the pressed state, because no primary family inverts its active rung for dark - the same package defect П2 records for danger.
AND A THIRD THING THE TOKENS SETTLE. The package state list is rest / hovered / active / read-only / disabled - there is no focused. Our theme paints .dx-state-focused AND .dx-state-active from one variable, so a keyboard user SITS at the value the package intends for a transient press. The button already separates them (bg-focused reads bg-primary-hovered). Splitting focus from active would leave the 1.62 where the package put it - under a finger, for the length of a click - and take the keyboard user to 4.30.
RE-CHECKED 15.09 against a freshly pulled Blazor, and the stem argument above was WRONG. Blazor's checked fills are content-primary-shared for primary but bg-success-shared and bg-danger-shared for the other two - I had read the INDETERMINATE variables, where the dash is a content-coloured mark, as the checked fills. So primary is the outlier inside Blazor, our bg family agrees with their success and danger, and our invalid MARK on content-danger-shared agrees with their indeterminate mark. There was no internal inconsistency.
WHICH LEAVES A CANDIDATE THAT SATISFIES BOTH SOURCES: bg-primary-shared*. The whole *-shared family is one value across bg, border and content, so it measures exactly like Blazor's content-primary-shared - mark 5.42 at rest and box 4.65 in dark against 3.36 and 2.88 today - while staying in the bg family Figma names, on the stem Blazor itself uses for success and danger. Light is identical to what ships now. The pressed rung still fails (2.31 / 1.98): no primary family inverts its active step for dark, which is П2's defect again.
RESOLVED 15.09, option 1. Focus now takes the HOVERED rung and the press keeps the package's active one, which is the shape the contained button already had (bg-focused reads bg-primary-hovered, bg-active reads bg-primary-active). The package state list justifies it: there is no focused state in it at all, so painting focus with the value meant for a click was never what the tokens asked for.
Four variables: -bg-focused and -border-focused moved down a rung, and -bg-active and -border-active were added to hold what the package assigns. The row that measured 1.62 split in two - the press keeps 1.62 on a state that lasts as long as a finger is down, and the focus a keyboard user SITS in went to 4.30, over the 3:1 a glyph needs. Light moves one step on focus, #003c70 -> #005397. Cascade verified on eight combinations: checked rest, hover, focus and press, the invalid pair, and the indeterminate pair including its ::before dash.
The fill STEM question is untouched and still open: bg-primary* as it ships, against bg-primary-shared* which reads 5.42 / 4.65 in dark where today it is 3.36 / 2.88.
STEM ACCEPTED 15.09. The checked fill moved from the plain bg-primary family to bg-primary-shared*. Light is pixel-identical at every rung - primary-100, 120, 120, 140 exactly as before - because the plain and shared families coincide in light. Dark improves everywhere: rest primary-100 -> 80, hovered and focused 90 -> 70, press 140 -> 120. The rest row left the contrast list (3.36 -> 5.42), hovered and focused left the state-pair list (4.30 -> 6.75), and the press went 1.62 -> 2.31 - still under 3, because the package gives no primary family an inverted active rung, which is П2 again.
Why the stem matters at all: the plain family does not know the mode. bg-primary is #0f6cbd in BOTH modes and bg-primary-active #003c70 in both, while the mark on them, content-inverted, does flip - to #161616 in dark. A fixed fill under a flipping mark is what produced 3.36 and 1.62. Every rung of the shared family flips.
CLOSED 15.09. All three parts are applied - the outline has its own role, focus is separated from the press, and the fill is on the shared stem. What is left below the floor is the press at 2.31 in dark, and no shipped role fixes it: every primary family keeps its active rung un-inverted for dark. That is the same package defect П2 files for danger, so it leaves the theme as a report rather than a question.

outlined-button-label.why: The outlined buttons - default, success, danger - hold their label on content-<hue> while the fill climbs bg-<hue>-subtler through hovered, focused, selected and active. The label is text, so the floor is 4.5, and no state after rest reaches it: hover and focus 4.02-4.43, selected 3.22-3.78, active 2.94-3.18 in light. Blazor climbs both sides - outline-primary-hover-color is content-primary-hovered and -active-color is content-primary-active - and measuring its pairing answers the question unevenly: content-primary-hovered on bg-primary-subtler-hovered gives 5.85 light / 5.11 dark, which clears AA in both and is a straight improvement on our 4.02 / 4.11; but content-primary-active on bg-primary-subtler-active gives 6.10 light / 2.05 dark, trading one mode for the other, and content-primary-selected does not exist at all. So: (1) adopt Blazor's hovered and focused rungs - provable, both modes, three roles; (2) for selected and active there is no shipped pair that passes, so either hold the fill still in those states or ask the package; (3) content-on-subtle-primary, which the package ships for exactly this surface and we never read, clears everything by a mile (10.82 / 16) but is neutral, not blue - it would stop the label being an accent. Recommendation: (1) now, (3) only if design wants a neutral label.

contained-button-label.why:
The filled default and success buttons, and the completed stepper indicator, put a white label on bg-<hue>-hovered and land at 4.18-4.21 in dark against the 4.5 a label needs. Light is 7.5-7.8, so this is dark-only. The foreground is content-static-dark, which is #ffffff in both modes by design, so the whole movement is in the fill: bg-primary in dark is #0f6cbd giving 5.38, and its hovered rung lightens to #2b7ecf giving 4.21. A hover that lightens is correct for dark; it is the amount that overshoots. Nothing in the theme can fix this - the pair is two package roles used exactly as intended - so this is a report to the design system, alongside the danger-content row already filed. Listed as a question only to confirm we file it rather than swap a role.
CLOSED 15.09: handed to the designers and left as it is. Nothing in the theme can move it - the pair is two package roles used exactly as intended - so the theme carries it as a known report rather than an open question.

items.why: Answered 14.09: if both lines are meant to be the same colour then two variables reading one role is fine, and the collapse is deliberate rather than a loss. Recorded so the audit does not reopen it. Worth noting what is NOT a problem here: the word accent in $scheduler-accent-border comes from the base layer, which names the parameter $scheduler-accent-border-color, and the theme takes its anatomy from base (NAMING M1). So the name is not lying about the theme - it is repeating the anatomy the markup already draws, which still has two lines even when they share a colour. Both variables stay: base needs two parameters, and a future theme may want them apart, as generic already does with 60% alpha against a 10% darkened edge.

items.title: scheduler: иконки формы встречи красятся bg-ролью, 1.56 в светлом
items.why:
The appointment form paints .dx-scheduler-form-subject-group .dx-scheduler-form-icon with --dx-scheduler-appointment-base-content, which reads bg-primary-subtle. In light that is primary-40 #b4d2f4 on the popup background #ffffff: 1.56 against the 3:1 a glyph needs. The role itself is right for what the variable mostly does - Blazor names the same role default-appointment-background-color, so bg-primary-subtle IS the appointment fill - but this variable is read by four different things: the appointment fill, the appointment marker, the focused-cell inset ring, and this icon. Legacy fluent does the same, but NFR-1 was retired on 15.09, so that no longer settles it. Options: (1) leave it, legacy parity; (2) split the icon off onto content-primary, which is 5.38 light / 4.65 dark, and accept a visible change in the appointment form; (3) split it off and keep the pale tint, which fixes the name but not the contrast. Recommendation: (2) if the form is meant to be usable, (1) if legacy parity outranks it - this one is genuinely a product call.
SHOWN IN THE REAL WIDGET 15.09, not reconstructed: a live dxScheduler on the built bundle, appointment form opened through showAppointmentPopup. The form has FOUR icons and they are read straight off the running page - the Subject icon is rgb(180,210,244) #b4d2f4 while the all-day clock, the repeat arrows and the description sheet are all rgb(68,68,68) #444444, which is content-subtle. So it is not a pale style for form icons: one icon out of four is the outlier, at 1.56 against the white form where its three siblings read 9.74. Dark is worse - the Subject icon becomes rgb(0,72,132) #004884 on a #242424 form while the others are #cbcbcb. With NFR-1 gone the recommendation stands without a counterweight: give the icon content-primary, 5.38 light and 4.65 dark, or content-subtle to match its three siblings exactly.
FIXED 15.09, and the fix turned out to be a DELETION rather than a swap. The form already had a general rule - .dx-scheduler-form-icon reads --dx-scheduler-form-icon, which is content-subtle, and that is where the other three icons get #444444. On top of it sat one more specific rule for the subject group alone, swapping in --dx-scheduler-appointment-base-content. Removing that override drops the icon back into the row with its siblings: 1.56 becomes 9.74 in light and the dark navy dot becomes #cbcbcb. No new name, one fewer special case, and the four-roles-in-one-variable problem loses one of its four readers. The glyph is a real icon (dx-icon-isnotblank, drawn as a filled circle by the font), not a colour swatch - its colour never tracked the appointment, so there was nothing accent-specific to preserve.

items.title: Кольцо и заливка мелкого контрола: одна анатомия, четыре решения
items.why:
Widened 09.09 when category Г was taken to the end. It started as radio versus checkbox and it is bigger: four controls paint the same anatomy - the ring of a small control plus its fill - and each resolves it differently. The checkbox splits it in two, border role on the ring and content role on the mark. The radio paints both from one variable on a border role but calls the variable bg. The read-only radio paints both from one variable on a CONTENT role, though no property is text. The slider does it twice with roles from different families - accent focused on a bg role, invalid focused on a border role - for the identical pair of properties. The treeView checkbox does it on a bg role and follows its own question. Nothing here is about pixels: the whole *-danger-shared family resolves to one value across bg, border and content in both modes. It is about which anatomy the family agrees on. Splitting is not free in code either - the radio rest-state variable is a parameter of dx-radiobutton-states-mixin in base, so splitting it changes a base signature and touches generic and material. ANSWERED 15.09 with option (1): the check box's shape everywhere, and the package settled what the shape is. core and vnext describe a radio in THREE slots - radio-button.color.checked.bg.rest = color.none, checked.border.* = border-primary-shared*, checked.icon.* = content-primary-shared* - so the disc has no fill at all, the ring is a border and the dot is an ICON, the same way a check box's tick is. blazor's set says the same for the invalid hue: radio.root.color.checked.invalid.icon = content-danger-shared, .border = border-danger-shared. Read-only is spelled out too: checked.border.read-only = border-disabled, checked.icon.read-only = content-disabled.
Every ring now has its own name on a border role and every dot its own name on a content role. The name keeps the slot word the property gives it (NAMING M3), so a dot stays -bg - it paints background-color - and only the role family follows what the element IS. That is the same reading the check box's invalid-mark-bg already carries.
The base mixin got what option (1) said it would cost: two optional parameters, $checked-border-color and $invalid-border-color, both defaulting to null and falling back to the single colour. generic and material pass neither, so their output is byte-identical.
Values: the radio does not move at all - primary-shared and danger-shared each resolve to one value across bg, border and content. The slider does, twice, and both are recorded in applied. The treeView member went away with Д22.

items.title: treeView всё ещё красит чекбокс по-своему в фокусе элемента
items.why:
The disabled overrides are gone. The focus block is not: when the treeView ITEM has focus, the checkbox inside it is repainted with three values of its own (treeView/_index.scss:18-72). They are not the checkbox own focus values: unchecked border goes to color-border where the checkbox uses bg-primary-active, unchecked fill goes to bg-low where the checkbox sets none, and the checked fill goes to bg-primary-hovered where the checkbox uses bg-primary-active. So three distinct divergences remain, and the rule stated for this widget - no unique checkbox styling in treeView - is not yet met. Removing the block is NOT value-neutral, which is why it was not done with the disabled one: legacy fluent carries the same block, so the pixel is inherited, not invented. There is a real argument for removing it beyond tidiness: the checkbox itself is not focused here, the item is, so painting the checkbox as focused states something untrue to a keyboard user. Options: (1) remove the block - the checkbox stops reacting to item focus, three variables and one public name go, etalons re-shoot; (2) keep the block but point its three values at the checkbox own focus roles, so treeView adds no roles of its own - still a pixel change, smaller; (3) keep as is for legacy parity. Note that (1) and (2) both collide with the checkbox-focused-fill question: whatever the checkbox focus fill becomes, this follows it. Recommendation: settle checkbox-focused-fill first, then (1).
CLOSED 15.09, option 1, once NFR-1 stopped holding it shut. Both blocks are gone and so are all four variables - the treeView no longer has a single colour name for the checkbox. Cascade checked on six scenarios: inside a focused item the checked box now resolves to check-box-icon-checked-bg and -border, the unchecked one to check-box-icon-bg and check-box-border, and a disabled one to check-box-border-disabled - all the checkbox own names, identical to a checkbox standing outside a tree. The select-all row still resolves to the checkbox FOCUS names, which is right: that element carries dx-checkbox itself, so there the checkbox really is the focused thing.
A dead name came out with it. $tree-view-checkbox-checked-border-focused existed only to feed $checkbox-border-color-focused in the base treeview-checkbox mixin - a parameter the base declares and never reads, so it painted nothing at all. The argument is null now; deleting the parameter belongs to the base owners.

items.title: Соседний виджет красит чужой контрол мимо тира - и перебивает его публичное имя
items.why:
Found 15.09 while answering what role the checkbox uses on hover. The checkbox itself moves only its border - border-contrast to border-contrast-hovered, the fill untouched - which is the same shape the tile uses and corroborates the Д6 answer. But the list repaints the same checkbox on ITEM hover, and it does it by importing the checkbox theme variable directly (list/_index.scss reads checkBoxColors.$check-box-icon-checked-bg-hovered), not through a name of its own. The variable holds ds.$color-bg-primary-hovered, so the compiled rule paints from var(--dxds-color-bg-primary-hovered) - the design-system name - with no component-tier name in between.
THE CONSEQUENCE IS DEMONSTRABLE, not theoretical. Checked with a cascade harness on the real bundle: a checked checkbox on its own resolves to var(--dx-check-box-icon-checked-bg-hovered), and the same checkbox inside a list with a selection decorator resolves to var(--dxds-color-bg-primary-hovered), because the list selector carries six classes against three. So overriding the checkbox's public name changes the control everywhere EXCEPT inside a list - the one place a consumer is least likely to test.
HOW WIDE. 230 colour declarations in the bundle paint straight from --dxds- with no tier name: color 32, background-color and the border colours the rest, concentrated in toolbar-menu-section (40), dataGrid (20), treeList (16), popup-content (10), menu-item (5), list (4). Sizes and typography do the same 510 more times, but that is by design - the tier is colour-first and the sizes sit on the scales on purpose. The colour half is not by design.
Thirteen theme files import a neighbour colour module inside _index.scss and paint with it directly; the same import inside a _colors.scss is harmless, because there it becomes the value of the widget's OWN tier name.
ANSWERED 15.09 with options (1) AND (2) together. Every read of a neighbour's colour module outside _colors.scss - 131 of them in 21 files - was rewritten to read that component's TIER name instead of its Sass variable, which is what put the design-system name in the bundle. All 131 already had a published name, so no name had to be invented for the conversion itself; (1) showed up as two places that had none: the cardView sort indicator, which was the one base mirror in its file still reading a role directly, and the dateRangeBox separator, which had been borrowing the text editor's -disabled name for a muted colour and now has its own.
Direct design-system colour paints in the bundle: 234 before, 47 after. Every one of the 47 is refused by the reachability gate for a reason it names: a portal (the grid and treeList revert tooltips and focus overlays, the scheduler appointment tooltip, the column choosers, the drag headers, the form dialog - the element is mounted outside its owner's root, so var() would resolve to nothing), or a scope outside the owner's roots that the runtime audit could not prove because the gallery never builds it.
Proof that nothing moved: a resolve-diff over both modes, 11676 rule-property pairs, expanding every var() chain to its final value. Exactly 17 differences, all inside the toolbar's overflow menu, all intended - see the applied rows. The runtime reachability audit on the built bundle reports no new holes, and all 49 non-fluent-next bundles are byte-identical.
23 scopes were added to nested-scopes.json, each proven by that runtime audit rather than asserted.

items.title: Точка радиокнопки осталась на семействе, которое не знает про режим
items.why:
The checkbox fill moved to bg-primary-shared* and the radio dot did not, so three concept groups opened the same day - checked bg rest, hovered and active, each with checkBox on the shared stem and radioButton on the plain one. This is not new damage: the radio has always read the plain family, which is mode-static, and the dot measures 2.88 against the page at rest in dark and 1.39 under a press, where a filled graphic wants 3.0. The shared stem gives 4.65 and 1.98 with light identical at every rung, exactly as it did for the checkbox. Options: (1) move radio-button-checked-bg* to bg-primary-shared* - the same move, the same cost, and the two controls stop disagreeing; (2) leave it and record the divergence, which means a form shows two sibling controls answering the same question differently. Recommendation: (1).
ACCEPTED 15.09, option 1. Applied.

items.title: treeView: фокус доходит до неактивного узла, а индикации нет
items.why:
Found 15.09 by keyboard, not by reading: arrow keys walk onto a disabled node - the tree does not skip it, aria-disabled is on the li and the node still takes dx-state-focused. In a tree WITH check boxes nothing is painted there. The focused-node rule excludes a disabled check box on purpose (its disabled paint must win), and the base mixin paints a focused background only for .dx-treeview-item-without-checkbox, so the row has nothing either. Measured on the built bundle: enabled node focused = check box border #005397 / #67a2e1; disabled node focused = #d7d7d7 / #4c4c4c, byte-identical to the same node unfocused. The variant WITHOUT check boxes does indicate it - the row takes bg-hovered #f5f5f5 / #3b3b3b, disabled or not. So one widget carries two different focus contracts and one of them has a hole. This is WCAG 2.4.7: the focus indicator disappears mid-list.
The package has no role for this and does not need one: there is no focus+disabled combination anywhere in the token set (global.color.focus / -inverted / -static / -static-inverted and global.border-width.focus, nothing state-crossed), because the design system marks focus with a separate OUTLINE rather than by recolouring the control. Blazor implements exactly that: treeview/layout.scss draws outline: var(--dxbl-treeview-item-focus-outline-width) solid var(--dxbl-treeview-item-focus-outline-color) on .dxbl-treeview-item-container:focus-visible, the colour being ds.$color-border-focus, and the same file explicitly zeroes the check box's own focus outline inside a tree (--dxbl-checkbox-focused-check-element-frame-outline-color: transparent). generic, material and legacy fluent all paint the check box instead, without a :not(disabled) guard, so they do show something - by painting a disabled control as if it were active.
Options: (1) give the with-checkbox variant the same focused row background the without-checkbox variant already gets (--dx-tree-view-bg-focused, bg-hovered) - one rule, no new role, closes the hole for every node and keeps the check box paint as an extra affordance for enabled ones; (2) move the tree onto the system focus rect (--dx-focus-rect-outline, already used by toolbar, dropDownMenu and pivotGrid) - Blazor's model exactly, but our rect is class-driven, so it would also show on a mouse click, where those three widgets gate it behind :focus-visible; (3) drop the :not(.dx-state-disabled) guard and paint the disabled check box, as the other three themes do - cheapest, and the reason it was added on 09.09 was precisely that it lies about a disabled control. Recommendation: (1) now, and (2) as part of the standing focus-ring question, which is where the package's four unused focus roles belong.
PRECEDENT INSIDE THE THEME, measured 15.09 on a live dxTabs: a disabled tab that takes focus KEEPS its focus mark. .dx-tabs.dx-state-focused .dx-tab.dx-state-focused paints background-color with no :not(.dx-state-disabled) guard, and the disabled rules beside it paint only color. Measured, in order: rest transparent / #161616, focused #f5f5f5 / #161616, focused+disabled #f5f5f5 / #ababab, disabled alone transparent / #ababab. So the focus mark is a background that says where you are, the disabled state is said by the content colour, and the two do not cancel.
And it is the same role: --dx-tabs-tab-bg-focused and --dx-tree-view-bg-focused both resolve to color-bg-hovered, #f5f5f5 light and #3b3b3b dark. So option (1) is not an invention - it is what this theme already does one widget over, on the very role the tree's without-checkbox variant already uses. That makes (1) the answer unless the product wants the focus ring question (3) first.
ANSWERED 15.09 with option (1): the with-checkbox variant now takes the same focused row background the without-checkbox variant already had - bg-hovered through --dx-tree-view-bg-focused, with the content colour and the item radius beside it - and the rule carries NO disabled guard, exactly as tabs carries none. The check box paint stays as the extra affordance for enabled nodes and keeps its :not(.dx-state-disabled), so a disabled control is never painted as active. Measured on the built bundle, both variants now read the same: focused node #f5f5f5 / #3b3b3b, focused DISABLED node #f5f5f5 / #3b3b3b with the text at #ababab / #767676 and the check box left at #d7d7d7 / #4c4c4c. The hole is closed for every node. Option (2), the focus rect, stays with the standing focus-ring question.

items.title: radioButton: фокус берёт ступень active и bg-роль для рамки - иначе, чем чекбокс
items.why:
Raised 15.09 from the running widget: a focused radio looks darkened. Measured, it is. The ring and the dot both read --dx-radio-button-checked-bg-active = bg-primary-shared-active: #003c70 light, #005397 dark. The check box reads the hovered rung after Д16 - border-primary-shared-hovered for the ring, bg-primary-shared-hovered for the fill: #005397 light, #67a2e1 dark. Two controls of the same family, two different rungs for the same state.
The dark mode is the defect. The primary ramp does not invert its active rung: bg-primary-shared goes #0f6cbd -> #4b90d9 between modes, hovered #005397 -> #67a2e1, but active only #003c70 -> #005397. So in dark the focused dot is #005397 on the #242424 surface = 1.98:1, below the 3:1 a non-text indicator needs, and WORSE than the same radio at rest (4.65) or hovered (5.79). Focusing makes the control harder to see - the same failure the tree's unchecked box had before 15.09. In light it goes the other way and is merely very dark: 11.17:1.
Two more findings in the same block. (a) Family: the ring is a border painted from a bg role. The check box was moved onto border-* for its border by Д16; the radio was not. (b) Dead declaration: $radio-button-icon-bg-focused (bg-alpha-hovered) is passed into the base mixin as the ripple colour, and fluent-next then kills the ripple - .dx-radiobutton-icon::after carries both content: "" and content: none in one rule, with width and height 0. The role is read, the reachability gate sees the read, and it paints nothing. The same call passes icon-border-read-only, hover and active into the ripple branch, where the @else that would have used them is not emitted at all.
Blazor answers the whole block the same way as the tree: focus there is an outline around the check element - checkbox-base.$focused-check-element-frame-outline-color = ds.$color-border-focus, width border-width-20, offset border-width-10 - and the control's own colours do not change on focus at all. Its rest and hover borders match ours exactly (color-border-contrast / -hovered), so the divergence is focus only.
ANSWERED 15.09 with option (1): the radio takes the check box's decisions. The ring reads a new $radio-button-checked-border-hovered / -focused / -active family on border-primary-shared*, the dot a new -bg-focused on bg-primary-shared-hovered, and focus is split out of the block it shared with the press, exactly as the check box splits them. Focus goes from the active rung to the hovered one: light #003c70 -> #005397, dark #005397 -> #67a2e1, so the dark ring leaves 1.98 for 5.79 and stops being worse than the same control at rest. The press keeps the active rung and its 1.98 in dark - that is the package's value for a state that lasts as long as a finger, and the check box was left the same way in Д16. Hover and press rings move from the bg family to the border family value-neutrally, since primary-shared is one value across both. The rest ring stays on the bg name: there one base mixin parameter paints both ring and dot, which is Д21. dxList followed - it mirrors both controls - and its check box border moved to the border family in the same pass. The dead $radio-button-icon-bg-focused is gone: the ripple it fed is switched off by content: none.

items.title: Невалидный контрол в фокусе: та же ступень active, тот же провал в тёмном
items.why:
Found 15.09 while applying Д26: the same shape on the danger ramp, and nobody has ruled on it. An invalid check box in focus reads bg-danger-shared-active / border-danger-shared-active, and the invalid radio reads $radio-button-invalid-bg-focused = border-danger-shared-active. That rung does not invert either: bg-danger-shared goes #c50f1f -> #e4554f between modes, hovered #9d0013 -> #ee726a, active only #76000b -> #9d0013. Measured on the built bundle: the invalid check box focused is #9d0013 on the #242424 surface = 1.81, against 4.22 for the same control at rest. Same failure as Д26, one ramp over.
Д16 moved the primary family to the hovered rung and left the danger family alone, because the question was the checked fill; Д26 moved the radio to the check box's decisions, and the check box's decision for invalid is the active rung - so the radio inherited it. Nobody chose it.
ANSWERED 15.09 with option (1), the symmetric fix, after validating the ramp on the built bundle: bg-danger-shared reads 6.07 light / 4.22 dark at rest, -hovered 8.60 / 5.36, -active 11.83 / 1.81. The active rung is the one that does not invert, exactly as on the primary ramp. Focus now takes the hovered rung on both controls - six names moved and six new -active names hold what the package assigns to a press: check box invalid bg, border and mark, radio invalid bg and border. The combined .dx-state-active, .dx-state-focused blocks were split the same way Д16 split them, so the press keeps its own value for the length of a click. Measured on the live invalid check box after the change: dark rest 4.22, hover 5.36, FOCUS 5.36 where it was 1.81, press 1.81; light 6.07 / 8.60 / 8.60 / 11.83

comment: Каждый вердикт - в одну и только одну секцию страницы. Таблица «решения не требуется» строится
отсюда и считается по данным: раньше это был литеральный массив в генераторе, и он уже разошёлся
с данными - graphic-ok печатался как 2, когда строк было 1, а graphic-ok-rest-only не попадал
никуда вовсе. Гейт держит равенство в обе стороны: вердикт без класса и класс без строк роняют
проверку, и сумма по секциям обязана сойтись с числом разобранных строк.
Класс заводится только когда строка с таким вердиктом есть в данных: пустой класс роняет гейт так
же, как неотнесённый вердикт. Поэтому spelling здесь нет - все три строки отвечены (answered).
graphic-ok-rest-only отсюда ушёл 15.09: он помечал строку, где покой брал порог, а состояние
нет. После перевода заливки на стем shared покой дошёл до 5.42, строка вышла из списка
контраста, и класс остался без единой записи - гейт это и поймал.
deferred-to ушёл 15.09 вслед за graphic-ok-rest-only: обе группы, которые он помечал,
закрылись сами - чекбокс и радиокнопка сошлись на одном стеме, а treeView перестал
красить чекбокс. Класс остался без строк, и проверка это поймала.
ring-and-fill ушёл 15.09: Д21 развёл кольцо и метку по отдельным именам, и все три строки, которые классом помечались, вышли из списка. Класс остался без записей - гейт это и поймал.
graphic-ok ушёл 15.09: единственной его строкой был белый знак на диске невалидного бейджа, и после перевода диска на bg-danger (Д14) пара вышла из списка контраста вовсе - 6.07 в обоих режимах.
graphic-ok вернулся 15.09: Д23 сделал видимыми пары, которые инструмент раньше не мог атрибутировать. Класс уходит и возвращается вместе со строками - в этом и смысл гейта.
